newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand weakened almost two cents on Monday in slow pre-Christmas dealings as an offshore order for dollars in the morning weighed on the thin market.
Dealers said the market was moving on tiny volumes with most players away for the festive season holiday break.
"The market is so thin it can move on orders of $20,000-30,000," one dealer said.
The rand touched a day's low of 4.6930 bid on the dollar on the back of an offshore order for dollars, which dealers said followed through from business late on Friday.
Traders said the order was linked to players squaring up their books for year-end, and expected more of the same activity for the few trading days left before the end of the year.
They said a thin stream of dollars coming into the market capped weakness on the local unit.
The rand ended to day at 4.6920/6970 from 4.6720/6770 at 1400 GMT Friday.

Traders said they expected more of the same listless activity on Tuesday, with the market closing early at 1000 GMT ahead of the Christmas and Family Day holidays on Wednesday and Thursday respectively. The market reopens again on Friday.
"The rand will probably hold in a 4.67-4.70 range for the rest of this week. We are really not expecting anything to happen," a trader said.
A break above the 4.70 level was unlikely, dealers said, with the central Reserve Bank seen adding liquidity to the market if this level was neared.
"A couple of exporters who have been sitting on the side will probably also come in at this level," another trader said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.8535/8665 from 7.7777/7907 against sterling and at 0.3305/3310 marks from 0.3324/3330.
On the bond market trading ground to a virtual halt with key gilts moving in tight ranges.
The benchmark R150 was stuck at Friday's 16.11 percent level amid a total lack of interest, dealers said.
"The market is stone cold dead," a dealer said, predicting a similar performance on Tuesday when the market will also close at 1000 GMT and remain shut on Wednesday and Thursday.

On the money market, there were signs of liquidity pressures easing as the daily shortage dipped back below 10 billion rand level on Friday and Saturday after touching an eight-month high of 10.904 billion rand last Wednesday.
Reserve Bank figures show the shortage at 9.969 billion on Saturday from 9.703 billion on Friday and 10.312 billion on Thursday.
Three-month NCD rates were steady at 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at a year high of 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners bought a net 2.19 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 14.68 million rand on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 2.43 billion rand on Friday from 2.71 billion rand on Thursday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
